modalLead: This is a big one. Health grew up: bookmarks can now be monitored on their own schedule, with uptime history, certificate expiry, drift detection and alerts when something goes down — plus a new Work through mode for clearing the list one bookmark at a time. There is a lot here, and most of it rewards five minutes of reading first: Config → Help → Health walks through the whole thing around one worked example, and the Health view offers the same tour the first time you open it. With this much new at once, something is bound to have slipped through — if you hit a bug, please report it on GitHub, it is the fastest way to get it fixed.

items.text: Monitor a bookmark. Press c on a row in Health, or right-click it, and choose Monitor. The server then checks it on its own interval — 5 minutes to 24 hours — whether or not you have the dashboard open, and the row grows a heartbeat bar, an uptime percentage and a response-time chart.

Say what "up" means for a page. A shop that answers with "Database connection failed" is up by every ordinary measure. Set Text the page must contain, or the status codes that count as healthy, and those failures get their own Content tile rather than being lost among the broken links.

Watch a page stop being the page you saved. Turn on Watch for redirects, retitling and rewrites and a bookmark that quietly starts pointing somewhere else — a lapsed domain, a moved article — gets a Moved, Retitled or Changed badge, even while it answers 200.
Certificate expiry. Every monitored HTTPS check already completes a TLS handshake, so the expiry date comes free. Rows carry a badge with the days left, and warnings go out at 30, 7 and 3 days.

Work through. Filtering to Broken tells you what is wrong and then makes you hunt for each row again after every fix. The Work through button — or f — puts one bookmark on screen at a time with its actions large: re-check, open, delete, skip. Esc leaves you on the row you reached.

Accept a change you meant to happen. A rebrand or a docs move trips drift on every bookmark pointing at that site at once. Tick them and use Accept drift to clear the lot — the next check records the pages as they are now.
One tidy row of filters. The common filters stay visible and the rest moved behind More, with their counts beside them.
A guided tour on first use. Opening Health for the first time walks you through setting up one monitored bookmark, start to finish. Replay it from Config → Behavior → General.

Pick your service. Rather than hand-writing a webhook body, choose Slack, Discord, Telegram, Gotify, ntfy or Pushover — each asks only for what it needs. Send test alert confirms it lands before you rely on it.

Quieten one bookmark. Tick Do not alert me about this bookmark and it is still checked and still shown as down — only the message is held back. The row says Muted so it is never mistaken for one that failed to warn you.

Maintenance windows. A service that restarts nightly is not broken. Set the days and times under Config → Behavior → Status & health and failures inside them raise no alert and do not count against uptime — while the checks still run and the heartbeat still records them.

One message when everything falls over at once. A host going down takes every bookmark behind it with it. Rather than a dozen near-identical alerts in a second, you get one naming the first few and counting the rest.

Undo works at the item limit. Undoing a delete in a full inbox used to report success and quietly drop the link — it looked restored until the next reload. The returning link is now kept, and if there is genuinely no room the undo says so.
A failed mark-read no longer reads as a success. When the save failed, the row greyed out anyway and a "marked read" message followed the error. Both now tell you the same thing.
Tags survive a capture. Tags sent when a link is saved are kept instead of being dropped on the way in.
